title: Checking isomorphisms on constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible, let
$F_1,F_2:\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$ be exact functors
preserving direct sums, and let $\eta:F_1\to F_2$ be a natural transformation
of exact functors. If $\eta_K$ is an isomorphism for every
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, then it is an isomorphism for every
$K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal T=D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$, $\mathcal S=\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, $\mathcal D=\Loc(\mathcal S)$ and $\mathcal T\prime=\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$. By [det-def-localizing-closure-existence], clauses 1 and 2 applied separately to $X$ and $Y$, $\mathcal T$ is triangulated with arbitrary small direct sums, and $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal T\prime$ are full replete triangulated subcategories closed under their ambient small direct sums. For a small family $(K_i)$ in either subcategory, its ambient coproduct belongs to that subcategory by closure. For every test object $L$ of the subcategory, fullness identifies the maps from that coproduct to $L$, and from each $K_i$ to $L$, with the ambient maps; the ambient coproduct universal property therefore remains the coproduct universal property in the subcategory. Thus both subcategories have the required small direct sums. By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], each of these full triangulated subcategories, with the shift and the distinguished triangles of $\mathcal T$ (resp. of $D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$) whose vertices lie in it, is itself a triangulated category, and its inclusion is exact; so $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal T\prime$ are triangulated categories with arbitrary small direct sums. These are exactly the module-object ambient categories and the defining localizing intersections of [sk-def-localizing-closure], in its fixed indexing universe. In particular $\mathcal D$ is the smallest such subcategory of $\mathcal T$ containing $\mathcal S$, and the functors in the statement have domain $\mathcal D$ and codomain $\mathcal T\prime$.

source.place: Statement and proof: the source and target localizing categories; ambient structures supplied by sk-def-localizing-closure-existence.md, clauses 1 and 2.

proof.text: Apply [det-sf-determination-localizing] with ambient domain $\mathcal T$, generator class $\mathcal S$, target $\mathcal T\prime$, and its explicitly allowed restricted functor domain $\Loc(\mathcal S)=\mathcal D$. Step 1 checks its triangulated-category, coproduct and localizing-closure premises. The functors $F_1,F_2$ are exact and preserve these sums by hypothesis. The phrase transformation of exact functors has precisely the shift-compatible meaning spelled out in that node: if $c_{a,K}:F_a(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F_a(K)[1]$ are the given shift isomorphisms, then $c_{2,K}\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]c_{1,K}$. Thus the cited lemma makes $\mathcal C_\eta=\{K\in\mathcal D:\eta_K\text{ is invertible}\}$ a triangulated coproduct-closed subcategory. The hypothesis of this item says $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal C_\eta$. Moreover $\mathcal C_\eta$ is closed under isomorphisms, since for an isomorphism $u:K\to K'$ in $\mathcal D$ naturality gives $\eta_{K'}=F_2(u)\eta_KF_1(u)^{-1}$; it is closed under sums taken in $\mathcal T$, because by Step 1 these are the sums in $\mathcal D$; and for a distinguished triangle of $\mathcal T$ with two vertices in $\mathcal C_\eta$ the third lies in the replete triangulated $\mathcal D$, hence is a triangle of $\mathcal D$, hence lies in $\mathcal C_\eta$. So $\mathcal C_\eta$ is one of the full replete triangulated subcategories of $\mathcal T$ intersected in [sk-def-localizing-closure], whatever repleteness convention is read into the minimality clause of the cited lemma. The final implication of the cited statement, equivalently this minimality, therefore gives $\Loc(\mathcal S)\subset\mathcal C_\eta$, which is the required invertibility at every $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. No extension of either functor to the ambient $\mathcal T$ is asserted or needed.
